steps.title: 01-signin: Sign in on the login form with email bench@example.com and password bench-pass-1234, then report what page you land on and what is visible

02-create: Create a new repair ticket titled exactly '{{runid}} RD Bench Ticket' using the New ticket button. Fill in any required fields the form demands (customer, description, etc.) with sensible values, and note which fields were required. Submit, wait for the ticket to appear/be saved, and report the ticket's reference (e.g. RD-xxxx), its status, and the customer you chose.

03-open: Open the ticket '{{runid}} RD Bench Ticket' (ref {{02-create.ticket_reference}}) from the ticket list. On its detail page, add a part named exactly '{{runid}} RD Part A' with cost 100 and markup 25. Fill whatever fields the add-part form has (name, cost, markup, quantity if present) and submit. Wait for the part to appear in the ticket's parts list. Report the part's name, cost, markup, quantity, and the price the app computes/displays for that part, plus any total shown for the ticket.

04-add: On ticket {{02-create.ticket_reference}}'s detail page ({{01-signin.url}}/{{02-create.ticket_reference}}), add a second part named exactly '{{runid}} RD Part B' with cost 200 and markup 25, quantity 1, using the Add part dialog. Submit and wait for the part to appear in the parts table. Report the new part's name, cost, markup, quantity, the price the app computes for it, and the ticket's parts total after adding it.

05-edit: On ticket {{02-create.ticket_reference}}'s detail page, edit the part named '{{runid}} RD Part A' so its cost changes from 100 to 150 (keep markup 25 and quantity 1). Use the part's edit control in the parts table. Save the change and wait for the parts table to reflect the new cost. Report the part's new cost, markup, quantity, the price the app now computes for Part A, and the ticket's parts total after the edit.

06-change: On ticket {{02-create.ticket_reference}}'s detail page, try to change the ticket's status to 'Ready' (there should be a status control — a combobox, dropdown, or status buttons). If the app refuses and shows an error or validation message, do NOT work around it yet — just report the exact refusal/error text shown, and any hints the page gives about what is required before the Ready status is accepted. Also report what statuses are available in the status control.
